style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: On a brushed-steel workbench in a machine shop, a compact matte clay metering assembly: three graphite tally-register modules in a row on a cast aluminum baseplate. A single flanged input rail enters from the left and splits into three short branch lanes, each leading to one module. The first module has an open safety-yellow gate that also counts a side handoff chute; the second has a one-way ratchet gate blocking the side chute; the third has no gate, a flat pass-through slot. Tiny blank count dials, moulding seams, and contact shadows. One directional key light rakes from the upper left, throwing long cast shadows. Bone white, graphite, safety yellow. Asymmetric off-centre composition, wide 16:9.

rationale: The story is structurally abstract—three vendors rewrite the unit definition on a pricing page—so a small physical assembly of gated counters states the metering logic directly without falling into datacenter or macro clichés.
